description:
## Background

`.config/wt.toml` currently installs dependencies with ambient `pnpm` during `pre-start`, trusts mise only in a background `post-start` hook, and runs separate pre-merge commands for `pnpm test` and `cargo check`. This ordering leaves a new worktree’s dependency installation outside the pinned toolchain and allows merges to skip linting, typechecking, formatting checks, Clippy, and Rust tests.

## What to build

Make Worktrunk use the same mise-managed toolchain and canonical gate as manual and git-hook workflows.

## Technical Approach

Update `.config/wt.toml` so:

- blocking `pre-start` runs `scripts/mise-exec.sh trust`, then `scripts/mise-exec.sh install`, then `scripts/mise-exec.sh x -- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`;
- `post-start` retains only ignored-file copying;
- `[pre-merge]` has one `gate` command invoking `scripts/mise-exec.sh run gate`.

Remove the old post-start trust hook and the separate test/Rust pre-merge commands.

Refresh Worktrunk project-command approvals after changing the hook commands. The user must review and approve them through `wt config approvals add`; agents must not bypass this security decision.

## Considerations

- Verify Worktrunk runs `pre-start` from the newly created worktree root and that `mise.toml` is present before the hook starts.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` still runs `prepare`, which installs Lefthook for the worktree.
- `scripts/mise-exec.sh` must work from Worktrunk’s shell environment without relying on interactive mise activation.
- `wt hook pre-merge` runs after rebase and before merge; the gate must therefore be read-only except for normal tool caches.
- The project’s `pnpm-workspace.yaml` contains an override and build-script policy. Do not accidentally bypass it in the repository-owned setup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new Worktrunk worktree trusts the config, provisions mise-managed tools, and installs dependencies with the pinned pnpm version before post-start work.
- [ ] `.config/wt.toml` has one pre-merge gate command and no separate ambient `pnpm test` or `cargo check` commands.
- [ ] `wt hook pre-merge` executes `mise run gate` and propagates failures.
- [ ] Worktrunk command approval is refreshed and documented.
- [ ] A fresh worktree does not depend on globally active Node, pnpm, Rust, rustfmt, or Clippy versions.

## Test Plan

- Create a disposable worktree with `wt switch --create` or the project’s normal workflow.
- Verify dependency installation and the resulting Node/pnpm versions.
- Run `wt hook pre-merge` and inspect its output/logs.
- Make a deliberate failing change and confirm pre-merge blocks it.
- Restore the change and confirm the same worktree passes.

## Triage

ready-for-agent

comments.text: Implemented in PR #69. wt.toml: pre-start is now an ordered mise pipeline (trust → install → mise x pnpm install --frozen-lockfile), post-start keeps only copy-ignored, pre-merge is the single canonical 'scripts/mise-exec.sh run gate'. Also added scratch/** to the canonical ignore policy (quality.ignores.ts) because copy-ignored copies gitignored scratch/ into every new worktree and ultracite check failed the gate on it — this failure existed on main too. Gate verified passing end-to-end in the worktree (exit 0) and failing on a deliberate format error (exit 1). PENDING USER ACTION: run 'wt config approvals add' to review/approve the changed hook commands; until then wt switch --create and wt hook pre-merge stop at the approval prompt. After approval, run 'wt hook pre-merge' once to close out the last acceptance criterion.

title: Migrate Worktrunk lifecycle and pre-merge validation
